Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: photorealistic medieval base-color material texture pair for a 1499 chapel vault. Create completely new content from this text only.
Primary request: ONE opaque RGB image with an exact 2:1 horizontal aspect ratio, ideally 4096 x 2048 pixels. The image is TWO full square material components placed directly side by side, each occupying exactly half the width and the full height. The left square is painted pale lime plaster. The right square is the matching unpainted pale lime plaster. There is no gap, gutter, frame, separator, border, label, or text. This is a technical texture master, not a scene and not a designed presentation board.
Left square: a flat close-up of authentic late-1400s lime plaster bearing a naturally repeating pattern of small thin leafy floral vignettes: fine reddish-brown and muted ochre stems, quiet muted green leaves, small faded flowers. The pigment is worn, gently flaking and translucent in tiny spots where the plaster is visible. Each vignette is isolated, delicate and complete, spaced in a regular loose repeating arrangement so the square can repeat horizontally and vertically. No long connected vines or broad central composition. The pattern repeats naturally with consistent spacing across the virtual tile boundary; leave the same ordinary plaster intervals between motifs at the edges as between motifs inside, no special edge band. Plaster tone and texture must stay uniform at the outer edges. The painting is opaque over the plaster; absolutely no alpha, cutout, or transparent background.
Right square: only bare unpainted plaster, precisely matching the left square's underlying warm pale ivory-gray lime plaster hue, grain, fine pitting, scale, and illumination. No trace of flowers, leaves, stems, ghosts, pigment or darker edge zones. Fine and evenly distributed microtexture, slight authentic age, no conspicuous stain or feature. Both halves must have the same plaster base, not two different materials or tones.
Composition/framing: orthographic, perpendicular camera facing the surface; both square components fill their entire allotted area, with no perspective or lens distortion. No vault architecture or curvature.
Lighting: absolutely even neutral diffuse light over every pixel, identical exposure and white balance in both halves. No shadow, center spotlight, gradient, vignette, darkening at edges, highlights, HDR, or theatrical lighting.
Style/medium: a realistic photograph of physical, gently worn matte plaster and faded medieval pigment; quiet restrained colors, not flat vector graphics, not crisp modern wallpaper. The two squares are seamless material tiles by natural pattern design, not by faded or blurry edge strips.
Avoid: people, faces, animals, objects, architecture, text, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, borders, panel lines, perspective, modern materials, saturated color, canvas weave, glossy paint, radial aging patches, any transparency. Output only the single 2:1 RGB texture master.

Some angular, some more rounded, tilted freely rather than stacked as rectangular blocks. Rough charcoal gray, black and dark brown soot coats the stones and recessed lime mortar, with patches of gray stone visible. Fine and medium heat fractures run irregularly through stone surfaces; strong authentic soot and heat weathering, no glowing hot areas.
